rationale: Roberts is likely to keep the opinion narrow and institutionally cautious, emphasizing the disjunctive text of § 1229a(b)(5)(C)(ii) and cabining Pereira/Niz-Chavez to the stop-time context. Kagan is the main alternative author because her reasoning is the majority’s textual core, while Gorsuch/Thomas have elevated concurrence risk to stress anti-surplusage/textualist themes and Sotomayor is likely to write a lone dissent grounded in Pereira/Niz-Chavez and notice-protective concerns.
